haiku-low.q1: They see the generic message: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is inserted or sent, with the same timing.
haiku-low.q2: The fourth request gets the generic message, with no link and no email. The user is not told why.
haiku-low.q3: A link works for 30 minutes after creation. It ends sooner if a newer link is issued for the account, or if it is used in a successful reset.
haiku-low.q4: The link stays live. The password check runs before the link is burned, so nothing is written, and it works until it expires.
haiku-low.q5: No devices stay logged in, since all the user's sessions are deleted, including the one that reset. The user must log in again with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with backoff, then logs an error and deletes the job. Nobody is told; the screen had said the email was sent.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is kept in the reset job in email_jobs with the user id and address. The worker builds the link from it and emails it.
haiku-low.q8: The page posts the token from the fragment to /check. The server hashes it, finds the row by token_hash, and applies the live test: unused, unsuperseded, unexpired.
haiku-low.q9: In password_reset_tokens, counting the user's rows created in the last 60 minutes, using an index on (user_id, created_at). Old rows fall out of the window, and a scheduled purge deletes rows older than 24 hours.
haiku-low.q10: In the same transaction as the new link, before COMMIT, the account's live older links get superseded_at set to now(), so they stop working.
haiku-low.q11: Password hash update, session deletion and the changed-password job insert all happen in one transaction before COMMIT. The worker sends the confirmation email afterward, from the queued job.
haiku-low.q12: A conditional UPDATE sets used_at only where the token is still live, returning user_id. Only one request gets a row; the other gets zero rows, rolls back and receives 410.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic message ("If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link."), same as for any address, with padded timing. Nothing is inserted and no email/job is queued, so nothing is sent.
sonnet.q2: The count of token rows in the last 60 minutes (rolling) is 3 or more, so the API commits, creates no link and sends no email. The user still gets the generic message and is not told why.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes from creation (expires_at). It ends sooner if a newer link is issued for the same account (superseded) or if it is used in a successful reset (burned).
sonnet.q4: Still live and unchanged. /complete returns 422 (weak or breached), nothing is written, and the link stays live until it expires.
sonnet.q5: None. All the user's sessions are deleted, including the device that did the reset, and no session is created. The user is redirected (303) to /login and logs in with the new password.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries with backoff up to 3 times, then logs an error and deletes the job. Nobody is told. The user saw "sent" but no email arrives, so they must request again (which counts toward the limit). A metric/alert is only proposed (open question 3).
sonnet.q7: The raw token is stored in the reset job in email_jobs. The worker builds https://<app>/reset#<token> from the job's raw token and the base URL setting and emails it to the job's recipient address. The job row is then deleted.
sonnet.q8: The token from the request body is hashed (SHA-256) and the row is found by token_hash (unique index). It is good if live: used_at IS NULL AND superseded_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now(). /check is read-only and returns {valid: true|false}.
sonnet.q9: It is not a stored counter. It is computed by counting rows in password_reset_tokens for the user with created_at in the last 60 minutes (any state), using the (user_id, created_at) index. Old requests drop out as the rolling window moves past them. A scheduled purge deletes rows older than 24 hours.
sonnet.q10: Within the same transaction as issuing the new one (after the rate-limit count passes, before inserting the new token row and job), the user's live links are marked superseded_at = now(). They stop working in the same commit that creates the new link.
sonnet.q11: In a single transaction: the token's used_at is set, users.password_hash is updated, all the user's sessions are deleted, and the changed-password job (holding only the user id) is inserted, then COMMIT. The confirmation email job is queued inside the transaction, after the password update and session deletion and before COMMIT. If anything fails before COMMIT, all of it rolls back.
sonnet.q12: The burn step is a conditional UPDATE setting used_at only where the token is live, with RETURNING user_id, inside the transaction. One submit gets 1 row and continues. The other gets 0 rows, rolls back and returns 410. (The earlier read is only a fast exit, not the guard.)
